Simple past vs Simple Present, Regular vs Irregular Verbs, in All Forms

You use simple present tense when you are referring to facts, routines or daily activities, on the other hand, we use the simple past tense when an event or action happened and finished in the past.

For past simple you may find that there are verbs which change totally partial or nothing, we call those irregular. irregular, there are also verbs which just add –ed –d or –ied in order to provide a past sense to the sentence which we call regular.

You use the present simple tense when you are referring to facts, routines, or daily activities; on the other hand, use the past simple tense when an event or action happened and finished in the past.

Every time you use the past simple tense, you have to bear in mind that there are regular and irregular verbs.

Keep in mind that the regular verbs end with the preposition –ed, -d, or –ied depending on the termination of the verb.

We classify the ends of the regular verbs as follows:

-d verbs end in silent e 

  • Close = closed
  • Dispose = disposed

-ied verbs end in vowel + y 

  • Study = studied
  • cry = cried

-ed verbs are all the other regular verbs 

  • Visit = visited
  • Show = showed
  • Work = worked

Irregular verbs, on the other hand, don’t have a specific rule or classification because they change partially or totally from their base form.

"Have to" And "Need to" to Express Absence of Necessity
You can use “have to” and “need to” in negative form to express that something is not necessary or mandatory to do.

We use “have to” and “need to” in their negative form when you want to express that something is not necessary. To do so, you have to use the following rule:

 Subject + don’t/doesn’t + have to/need to + verb (base form) + complement.


Examples: 
You don’t need to always use .Net Framework to develop apps; however, you don’t have to change the programming language either.


As you can see, in the previous example the use of need to and have to in their negative forms express a lack of necessity or obligation.
Since all of our computers work with Windows, we don't need to use other programming platforms, our development department only uses Microsoft .Net framework

Trainer: Hey, welcome to the company.
Trainee: Thank you very much.
Trainer: I'm going to be your guide and trainer today. Tell me; did you ever work with Microsoft .Net framework in your previous job?
Trainee: No, I didn’t. In the company where I worked before, we didn't have to use it at all. Sorry.
Trainer: You don't need to worry about it. We are helping you to get used to it during your first days.
Trainee: Thanks a lot, I really appreciate it.

Trainer: Since all of our computers work with Windows, we don't need to use other programming platforms, our development department only uses Microsoft .Net framework, as it is a consistent programming platform that allows a wide but clear set of solutions to all the needs that programming and managing applications may have. 
Trainee: It seems to be very practical.
Trainer: Yeah, it is. Its versatility allows programmers to use codes from different programming languages, such as C++ or C#, without major complications. We know this feature as Language Interoperability. Now, we can say that among its many features, there are some that you must learn; for example, there is the Common Language Runtime feature that allows apps and programs run within windows, as it provides such programs with the necessary codes to do so. However, there are some other features we are not checking right now, due to the little time we have, but that are important to take into account, like the Base Class Library and the ASP and ADO .NET class frameworks, which are large libraries consisting of useful and essential collections of classes, interfaces, and value types.

Trainee: Wow, I think that's a lot of information, and honestly, I didn't understand it very well.
Trainer: As I told you, you don't have to worry about it right now. In fact, I bet you can learn much more by actually getting to use Microsoft .Net Framework.
Trainee: Sure, I think it is easier for me if there is an opportunity to get familiar with it and understand better how to use it.
Trainer: Ok, follow me. She is Carol. Carol understands perfectly how this works, she can help you.
